latents roadmap

Source: ROADMAP.md

Rewritten 2026-09-28. Models come first: new model families and extensions of the existing ones, ahead of inference refinements, workflow reach and infrastructure. Every item keeps the package rule that whatever ships is defensible: an independent likelihood check, parameter recovery by simulation, interval coverage where standard errors are reported, and classed refusals for what is not supported.

Size is a rough guide: S under half a day, M one to two days, L several days or dependent on outside material.

Evidence for existing claims: validation/MATH_AUDIT.md, equivalence/houle-2026/REPORT.md, validation/*.R and equivalence/.

Next (set 2026-10-17, after 0.9.37)

Owner priority remains growth, transitions and lta(). Each item ships with its evidence (an external reference, a simulation, or both).

Priority E — Equivalence 2.0 (plan, set 2026-10-17)

Owner priority: equivalence is to be very strong. The suite has breadth (Mplus, Latent GOLD, mclust, lcmm, flexmix, depmixS4, tidySEM, tidyLPA; 700 expectations at 0.95.0) but the work of 2026-10-17 exposed three weaknesses:

  • Tests that could not fail. Every group-level statistic replaced by a perfect 1 still passed 26 of 26 expectations, because the two-level references are so well separated that everything prints as 1.000.
  • Tests that passed for the wrong reason. AvePP matched by sorting apart from the class alignment; reference ids unchecked; run.sh reusing stale outputs; a two-level count parser reading the joint-pattern table.
  • Gaps no test covered. Rows with nothing observed were counted in entropy for several releases: no reference dataset had such a row, and the Mplus helper computed entropy itself instead of reading the package’s value.

Resources on this machine: genuine Mplus 9 Demo (/Applications/MplusDemo/mpdemo) and Latent GOLD 6.1 under Wine (~/.wine-latentgold), both run in batch; simulab 0.4.10 (../simulab), whose generators store the true parameters with every dataset (simulate_lpa(), simulate_ml_lpa(), simulate_lca(), simulate_hmm(), simulate_markov(), simulate_growth(), inject_missingness() with MCAR/MAR/MNAR, apply_batch()); and JStats (../JStats/validation/r-reference/), 95 genuine Mplus mixture outputs, 62 with their data file, of which 4 transition fixtures are used so far.

Constraint to verify first: the Mplus Demo limits model size (number of dependent variables and covariates); configurations beyond it need a full licence or Latent GOLD alone.

Order: E2.1 (where to aim), then E2.2 and E2.7 (tests that can fail), then E2.3 with E2.4 and E2.5 (the main body), then E2.6, E2.8 and E2.9.

Open (each M): Houle families against Mplus; lta() order 2, mover-stayer, occasions = "grid", full covariance, ordinal and count; mixture_regression() negative binomial, ordinal and two-level beyond one class; three_step() and r3step() robust SEs and group level; parameter_inference(method = "bootstrap"); pool_imputations(); fit_staged(); sensitivity().

Found and fixed by Equivalence 2.0

  • lta() general engine: the quasi-Newton finish stopped early near a boundary (factr tied to tol since 0.9.13); LMest occasion model off by 1e-4 in transitions. Fixed (factr = 10, as in 0.9.1).
  • r3step(): BFGS from zero settled on a separation ridge (Mplus ex7.3); latents_no_converge. Fixed (second start from the proportional estimate).
  • Comparisons kept as scripts could not fail the suite; the Latent GOLD kit compared against saved targets. Fixed (tests, live targets).
  • enumerate_classes(cores = ) on macOS with Accelerate BLAS: forked workers segfaulted once the session had used BLAS, and a worker killed by a signal came back as an empty candidate. Fixed (socket cluster where forking is unsafe; lost workers raise latents_parallel_failure).
  • The documentation claimed plain EM follows Mplus’s path from the same start; untested, so narrowed to mclust’s, which is tested.

New item from Equivalence 2.0

Rules for every item: the reference output is genuine and retained with its inputs and version; the comparison reads the package’s reported values, never a formula written in the test; class alignment uses one relabelling chosen from the posteriors and reused for every class-level quantity; ids are checked unique and complete; and each new test is shown to fail on a deliberate defect before it is accepted.

Priority 1 — Models

1.1 Multilevel model families (Houle et al.)

The core model has the dispersion-heterogeneity structure. The other five families need explicit identification constraints, a simulation recovery study each, and ideally Mplus runs as the oracle; the published supplement is ambiguous on syntax and parameter counts, so it cannot be the oracle alone.

1.5 Mixture regression (mixture_regression())

1.6 Growth models (latent class growth and growth mixture models)

Status (2026-10-02). Latent class growth analysis (group-based trajectories, Nagin) already works through mixture_regression(y ~ time, data, n_classes, id = "id", class_level = "group") for Gaussian, binomial and Poisson outcomes. It matches lcmm::hlme without random effects: log likelihood -2857.281151 vs -2857.281176, same estimates up to class order (300 persons x 6 occasions, 3 classes). Growth mixture models (random intercepts/slopes within classes, hlme(random = ~ time)) are not supported.

Interface (decided before coding). One verb, named arguments: extend mixture_regression() rather than add a function. random = ~ 1 + time (within-class random effects; default NULL keeps today’s model), random_covariance = c("varying", "equal", "proportional") (class-specific, common, or common times a class scale, the lcmm nwg), random_diagonal = FALSE (lcmm idiag), and later residual_correlation = c("none", "ar1", "brownian"). A growth mixture model needs id and class_level = "group"; anything else is refused by class.

References. lcmm::hlme 2.2.1 (installed; exact for Gaussian, no integration) and Latent GOLD 6.1 Syntax (installed under Wine; latent growth and mixture growth models with CFactors, Syntax Guide sections 5.3.4-5.3.5 and 5.4.3; quadrature, so evaluate our exact likelihood at its estimates before calling a gap a disagreement).

Phases (each ships only with its evidence; sizes as at the top):

Order: G0 -> G1 -> G2 -> G3 -> G4 gives a releasable Gaussian growth mixture model in about 4 working days; G5 next; G6 only with a concrete need. Risk: convergence with random-effect variances on the boundary or weakly separated classes may add a day to G1-G2.
